title: Computer Vision
objectives: This course introduces the fundamental concepts, methods, and applications of computer vision and digital image analysis. Students learn how images are represented and processed in digital systems; understand the relationship between image processing, human vision, and computer vision; apply spatial- and frequency-domain filtering and enhancement techniques; analyze image histograms, transforms, features, textures, and regions; and use classical algorithms for edge detection, shape detection, segmentation, recognition, and classification. The course also introduces machine-learning and deep-learning approaches to computer vision, practical vision applications, common environmental and imaging challenges, and hardware considerations for implementing computer-vision systems.
syllabus:
1. Introduction to Digital Image Processing and Computer Vision: Traditional vs. digital imaging; analog-to-digital image conversion, sampling, and quantization; digital image representation, binary, grayscale, color, and indexed images; image contrast, color models, and color-image representation; relationship between image processing, human visual perception, and computer vision; applications and fundamental challenges.
2. Spatial and Frequency Domain Image Enhancement: Digital image characteristics; spatial-domain and frequency-domain processing; image resolution and common representations (binary, 2.5D, and 3D images); image enhancement, sharpening, blurring, and restoration; spatial filtering, convolution, kernels, and neighborhood operations; smoothing and noise reduction (Gaussian, average, median, minimum, and maximum filters); frequency-domain filtering, Fourier transform, and wavelet transform for image analysis.
3. Histogram Analysis, Image Formats, and Compression: Grayscale and color-image histogram calculation, histogram equalization, and histogram-based analysis; image formats, encoding, and compression concepts; image degradation models, motion blur, and restoration techniques; software tools and libraries (MATLAB, Python, OpenCV).
4. Morphological Processing and Texture Analysis: Image morphology, structuring elements, and common morphological operations; texture analysis and texture-based image processing; image registration and spatial alignment methods.
5. Edge Detection and Image Segmentation: Classical computer vision algorithms including Canny edge detection, Hough transform for lines and circles, and template matching; segmentation concepts, region separation, thresholding, and practical segmentation methods.
6. Feature Extraction, Object Recognition, and Learning: Computer vision pipeline (preprocessing, feature extraction, decision making, classification); feature selection, feature extraction, and image descriptors; statistical methods and advanced approaches based on Bayesian inference; machine-learning and deep-learning algorithms for computer vision; Kalman and particle filtering for visual tracking.
7. Computer Vision Applications: Industrial quality control, automated PCB inspection, and visual defect detection; autonomous vehicles, drones, robotics, and gesture-based control; medical imaging, disease analysis, edge-based diagnosis, and feature visualization; biometric systems including face detection, facial expression and emotion analysis, age and gender estimation, vein, gait, iris, and fingerprint recognition; optical character recognition (OCR) for Persian and English, license-plate recognition, digital signatures, and barcode reading.
8. Implementation Challenges and Hardware Architectures: Handling environmental challenges including illumination and background changes, occlusion, scale variation, blur, and viewpoint variation; hardware requirements, embedded vision platforms, and hardware architecture comparisons for computer vision algorithms.
textbooks: 1. Fundamentals of Computer Vision (مبانی بینایی کامپیوتر), Dr. Mehdi Seyfi Pour, Dibagaran Tehran Publishing, 1st Edition, 1402 (2023/2024).
